mainTopic: Which animals' fat is excluded from נבלה impurity, how far רבי מאיר's ruling about pinched birds reaches, the status of the עגלה ערופה, and the opening of the new פרק on mixed sacrifices.
overview: The ברייתא finishes working out which animals' fat the פסוק about נבלה and טרפה is talking about. The word טרפה rules out non-kosher animals, and 'you shall not eat it' rules out a kosher חיה, so only a kosher בהמה is left. רבא explains to רב יעקב בר אבא that the end of the ברייתא is about a non-kosher bird, so a non-kosher animal's carcass is still טמא. The גמרא then returns to רבי מאיר's ruling in the משנה. רבי יוחנן limits it to unblemished birds, while רבי אלעזר extends it to blemished birds and even to geese and chickens. רבי ירמיה asks whether breaking a goat's neck would work the same way. רב דימי explains that the question assumes the עגלה ערופה itself is טהור, because the Torah speaks of כפרה with it. רב נתן challenges this from a ברייתא about its fat, and the גמרא answers that the ברייתא is about a calf that died, which leads to the rule that the calf becomes forbidden once it goes down to the valley. The פרק ends with הדרן, and a new משנה begins about sacrifices mixed with forbidden animals; its second case continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The ברייתא is stuck between two lines of reasoning
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא admits that one line of reasoning points to kosher animals and the other points to non-kosher animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you reason one way, the rule is about a kosher animal. If you reason the other way, it is about a non-kosher animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא is in the middle of a discussion and says that two opposite arguments both seem to work. It is setting up the next move, where a פסוק will decide between them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is which animal's fat the פסוק has in mind when it says the fat of a נבלה stays טהור. Both directions were argued just before this line, so logic alone cannot settle it. That is why the ברייתא now needs a word in the פסוק to decide.

keyTerms.meaning: In this way, meaning by this line of reasoning
A kosher animal
A non-kosher animal

phrases.english: When one approaches it this way,
it is about a kosher animal,
and when one approaches it that way,
it is about a non-kosher animal;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from the previous part of the דף, summing up a stalemate between two arguments.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the purity of the fat of a נבלה said about kosher animals or about non-kosher animals?

steps.title: The word טרפה shows the verse means kosher animals
steps.stepSummary: The word טרפה in the פסוק shows it is talking about a species where the law of טרפה applies, which means kosher animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'טרפה.' That means an animal whose species can be a טרפה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא settles the stalemate with a word in the פסוק. The word טרפה only makes sense for an animal that would be allowed to eat if it were healthy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A non-kosher animal is forbidden to eat no matter what, so calling it a טרפה adds nothing. Since the פסוק uses the word טרפה, it must be talking about a kosher species. So the non-kosher animal is left out.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק teaches; the formula that brings a verse to settle a question
An animal with a fatal defect, forbidden to eat even after proper שחיטה
In its species

phrases.english: the verse states: 'tereifa' —
one whose species has the law of tereifa.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1 using a word in the פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק is about kosher species, since only they can become a טרפה.

steps.title: But a kosher wild animal can also be a tereifa
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא objects: the word טרפה rules out non-kosher animals, but a kosher חיה can also be a טרפה, so it should still be included.
steps.simpleTranslation: I will leave out the non-kosher animal, since its species cannot be a טרפה. But I will not leave out the חיה, since its species can be a טרפה!
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a new problem with the answer it just gave. The word טרפה is not narrow enough to leave out a kosher wild animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The test from step 2 was 'a species that can be a טרפה.' A kosher חיה, like a deer, passes that test. So the word טרפה alone would wrongly include the חיה.

keyTerms.meaning: I will exclude, meaning leave out of the rule
An undomesticated animal, such as a deer

phrases.english: I will exclude the non-kosher animal,
since tereifa does not apply to its species,
but I will not exclude the undomesticated animal,
since tereifa does apply to its species!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reach of the answer in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The use of the word טרפה as the dividing line
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A kosher חיה can also be a טרפה, so the word טרפה cannot leave it out.

steps.title: 'You shall not eat it' leaves out the wild animal
steps.stepSummary: The words 'you shall not eat it' show the פסוק means an animal whose fat is forbidden but whose meat is permitted. That leaves out the חיה, whose fat is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'but you shall not eat it.' That means an animal whose fat is forbidden while its meat is permitted. This leaves out the חיה, whose fat and meat are both permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own problem with another phrase from the same פסוק. Now only a kosher בהמה fits.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק forbids eating this fat, which only makes sense where the fat is forbidden and the meat is not. A kosher חיה's fat may be eaten, so it does not fit. The rule is therefore narrowed to a kosher domesticated animal.

keyTerms.meaning: Its fat, meaning the forbidden fats (חלב)
Its meat
Excluded, meaning left out

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא uses two words in the פסוק. 'טרפה' rules out non-kosher animals, and 'you shall not eat it' rules out a kosher חיה. Only a kosher בהמה is left.

phrases.english: The verse states: 'but you shall in no way eat it' —
one whose fat is forbidden and whose meat is permitted,
excluded is an undomesticated animal,
whose fat and meat are both permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The rule is limited to an animal whose fat is forbidden but whose meat is permitted, which leaves out the חיה.

steps.title: Does a non-kosher animal's carcass not cause impurity?
steps.stepSummary: רב יעקב בר אבא asks רבא: if the ברייתא limits this to kosher animals, it seems only a kosher animal's נבלה makes things טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יעקב בר אבא said to רבא: If so, then only the carcass of a kosher animal makes things טמא, and the carcass of a non-kosher animal does not?!
steps.whatsHappening: A student challenges the way the ברייתא seems to read. He thinks it leads to a result that cannot be right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא keeps narrowing the פסוק down to kosher animals. רב יעקב בר אבא thinks this makes it sound as if the impurity of a נבלה only applies to kosher animals. But everyone knows that a non-kosher animal's carcass is also טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: But now, if so; a phrase that pushes an idea to an extreme result
A carcass, an animal that died without proper שחיטה
Makes things ritually impure (טמא)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב יַעֲקֹב בַּר אַבָּא לְרָבָא:
phrases.english: Rav Ya'akov bar Abba said to Rava:
If that is so,
it is the carcass of a kosher animal that imparts impurity,
but the carcass of a non-kosher animal does not impart impurity?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ברייתא's conclusion by showing where it seems to lead.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's limiting of the passage to kosher animals
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the subject is only kosher animals, it seems a non-kosher animal's נבלה would not make things טמא, which is known to be false.

steps.title: רבא: the end of the ברייתא is about a non-kosher bird
steps.stepSummary: רבא scolds him for a reading that has misled many elders. He explains that the end of the ברייתא is only about the carcass of a non-kosher bird.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: How many elders have you led into error with this! The end of the ברייתא is talking about the carcass of a non-kosher bird.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא rejects the student's reading. The part of the ברייתא that sounds as if it removes impurity is about a non-kosher bird, not a non-kosher animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A non-kosher bird's carcass does not make things טמא, so the ברייתא can leave it out. A non-kosher animal's carcass still makes things טמא. The ברייתא never said otherwise.

keyTerms.meaning: Elders, older scholars
You have caused to err, led astray
The latter clause, the end of a source
A non-kosher bird

steps.confusionAlert: Don't conclude that a non-kosher animal's carcass is טהור. רבא is saying it is טמא. Only the non-kosher bird is the case that does not make things טמא.

phrases.english: He said to him:
How many elders have you misled with this!
phrases.notes: רבא is scolding him: this mistaken reading of the ברייתא has already tripped up many older scholars.

phrases.english: In the latter clause we have come to the carcass of a non-kosher bird.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case of the end of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to say a non-kosher animal's carcass is not טמא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The end of the ברייתא is about a non-kosher bird, whose carcass is not טמא. A non-kosher animal's carcass still makes things טמא.

steps.title: How far does רבי מאיר's ruling of purity go?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says רבי מאיר ruled the bird טהור only when it was unblemished. רבי אלעזר says he ruled it טהור even when it was blemished.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: רבי מאיר ruled it טהור only for unblemished birds, not for blemished ones. רבי אלעזר said: even for blemished ones.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה. Two אמוראים argue about how far רבי מאיר's ruling of purity reaches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן limits רבי מאיר's ruling to birds that are fit to be offered. רבי אלעזר says the ruling covers blemished birds too, even though they could not be offered.

keyTerms.meaning: He ruled it ritually pure (טהור)
Unblemished, fit for a קרבן
Blemished, unfit for a קרבן

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows whether רבי מאיר's ruling depends on the bird being fit for the מזבח, or whether it reaches further.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan says:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא טִיהֵר רַבִּי מֵאִיר אֶלָּא בִּתְמִימִין,
phrases.english: Rabbi Meir deemed pure only unblemished birds,
phrases.notes: This goes back to the משנה: a bird killed by מליקה that turned out to be a טרפה, which רבי מאיר says does not make things טמא.

phrases.english: but not blemished ones.
And Rabbi Elazar says:
Even blemished ones.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא טִיהֵר רַבִּי מֵאִיר אֶלָּא בִּתְמִימִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, going back to the משנה's ruling of רבי מאיר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן says רבי מאיר's ruling of purity covers only unblemished birds. רבי אלעזר says it covers blemished birds too.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר's view reported again, even for geese and chickens
steps.stepSummary: A second report, from רב ביבי, backs up רבי אלעזר's view. It adds that רבי מאיר ruled טהור even for geese and chickens.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also stated: רב ביבי said in the name of רבי אלעזר: רבי מאיר would rule blemished birds טהור, and even geese and chickens.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another report that supports רבי אלעזר. This report stretches רבי מאיר's ruling even further.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Geese and chickens are not birds that may be brought as a קרבן at all. Even so, this report says רבי מאיר still ruled them טהור. So his ruling does not depend on the bird being fit for the מזבח.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also stated; brings a second report that supports a view
Geese
Chickens

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן limits רבי מאיר to unblemished birds. רבי אלעזר, backed by רב ביבי's report, extends it to blemished birds and even to geese and chickens.

phrases.english: It was also stated:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב בִּיבִי אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר:
phrases.english: Rav Beivai says that Rabbi Elazar says:

phrases.aramaic: מְטַהֵר הָיָה רַבִּי מֵאִיר בְּבַעֲלֵי מוּמִין,
phrases.english: Rabbi Meir would deem blemished birds pure,
and even geese and chickens.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי אלעזר's view from step 7 and stretches it further.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אלעזר's view that רבי מאיר ruled blemished birds טהור
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב ביבי's report in the name of רבי אלעזר, which includes even geese and chickens

steps.title: What if someone breaks a goat's neck?
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה asks whether breaking a goat's neck works like pinching a bird's neck, so that the goat would not be טמא as a נבלה. He gives reasons for both sides.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה asked: if someone broke the neck of a goat, what is the law? Maybe geese and chickens are טהור only because they are kinds of birds, like the birds whose necks are pinched, and a goat is not the same kind as a calf. Or maybe it is enough that a goat is a kind of farm animal, like the calf.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה extends רבי מאיר's ruling to a new case. He asks whether breaking a goat's neck keeps it from being a טמא נבלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah has a neck-breaking procedure for one animal: the עגלה ערופה, a young calf. One possible reason רבי מאיר stretched pinching (מליקה) to geese and chickens is that they are birds too. The question is how close the match must be: does the animal need to be the same kind as a calf, or is being a farm animal (בהמה) close enough?

keyTerms.meaning: Asks a question that is left open for now
Broke the neck from the back
The calf whose neck is broken when a murdered person is found and the killer is unknown
Or perhaps; brings in the other side of the question
Kind or type of creature

steps.confusionAlert: This question only makes sense inside רבי מאיר's view as רבי אלעזר explains it in Step 8, where רב ביבי reports that pinching works even for geese and chickens, which can never be brought as a קרבן. רבי ירמיה is asking how far that idea goes.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya asked:
If he broke the neck of a goat, what is the law?
phrases.notes: He means: is the goat now safe from being a טמא נבלה, like the pinched bird in רבי מאיר's ruling?

phrases.english: Geese and chickens, what is the reason they are טהור?
Because they are a kind of bird,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל עֵז לָאו מִינָא דְּעֶגְלָה נִינְהוּ;
phrases.english: but a goat is not the same kind as a calf;
or perhaps it is a kind of farm animal, and that is enough?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes רבי מאיר's broad ruling about geese and chickens from Step 8 and tests it on an animal's neck-breaking.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does breaking a goat's neck stop it from being a טמא נבלה, given that a goat is a farm animal but not the same kind as a calf?

steps.title: אביי notices a hidden assumption
steps.stepSummary: When רב דימי repeats רבי ירמיה's question, אביי points out that the question assumes the עגלה ערופה itself is טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב דימי was sitting and saying this teaching. אביי said to him: does that mean the עגלה ערופה is טהור?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי stops רב דימי to check something. The question about the goat only works if the עגלה ערופה itself is not a טמא נבלה, and אביי wants to know if that is really true.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ירמיה compared the goat to the עגלה ערופה. That comparison only helps if breaking the calf's neck keeps the calf טהור. אביי is surprised and asks for that starting point to be confirmed.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching or ruling being passed along
By inference; it follows from this that
Not טמא; here, it does not make things טמא as a נבלה

phrases.aramaic: יָתֵיב רַב דִּימִי וְקָאָמַר לַהּ לְהָא שְׁמַעְתָּא,
phrases.english: Rav Dimi was sitting and saying this teaching,
phrases.notes: This teaching is רבי ירמיה's goat question from Step 9.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
Does it follow that the calf whose neck was broken is טהור?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Checks the assumption hiding behind רבי ירמיה's question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the עגלה ערופה itself really טהור and not a טמא נבלה?

steps.title: Yes, because the calf brings atonement like קדשים
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי confirms that the עגלה ערופה is טהור. He quotes the school of רבי ינאי: the Torah uses the word כפרה for it, just as it does for קדשים.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Yes. The school of רבי ינאי say: the Torah writes atonement about it, as it does about קדשים.
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי answers אביי: yes, the עגלה ערופה is טהור. He gives the reason from the school of רבי ינאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah uses the word כפרה about the עגלה ערופה. That makes it like the קדשים, where a bird whose neck is pinched the proper way is not a טמא נבלה. So breaking the calf's neck counts like that proper pinching and keeps it טהור.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes
The study hall or school of רבי ינאי
Atonement
Animals set aside as holy offerings

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the next move. If the עגלה ערופה is treated like a קרבן for טומאה, then a source that treats it as a regular נבלה would challenge רב דימי. That is exactly where רב נתן is heading.

phrases.english: He said to him: Yes,
for the school of Rabbi Yannai say:
Atonement is written about it, as with holy offerings.
phrases.notes: The word כפרה about the עגלה ערופה is in דברים 21:8.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִין, אָמְרִי דְּבֵי רַבִּי יַנַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's question with a yes and gives the source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The עגלה ערופה is טהור, because the Torah speaks of כפרה with it, as it does with קדשים.

steps.title: רב נתן begins an objection from the fat of an עגלה ערופה
steps.stepSummary: רב נתן brings a ברייתא. It learns from 'you shall not eat it' that forbidden fat is טהור, then asks how we know this also applies to the fat of a שור הנסקל and an עגלה ערופה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נתן, father of רב הונא בר נתן, raised an objection: 'you shall not eat it.' This teaches only about fat that is forbidden to eat but allowed for benefit. From where do we learn the same about the fat of an ox that is stoned and of an עגלה ערופה?
steps.whatsHappening: רב נתן starts a challenge against רב דימי by quoting a ברייתא. The quote is not finished yet; this line sets up the question, and the punchline comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא learns from the פסוק that forbidden fat (חלב) does not become טמא as נבלה. The פסוק directly covers only fat you may not eat but may still use. So the ברייתא asks how we know this also covers fat from animals you may not use at all, like a שור הנסקל or an עגלה ערופה. Putting the עגלה ערופה in a discussion about נבלה טומאה looks like trouble for רב דימי's claim that it is fully טהור.

keyTerms.meaning: Forbidden fat of an animal
Benefit or use, such as selling or using something
An ox stoned by the court for killing a person
From where do we know this?

steps.confusionAlert: Don't expect the full objection here. The ברייתא's own question 'מנין' is only the opening. The ברייתא answers it in Step 13, and the actual challenge to רב דימי comes in Step 14.

phrases.aramaic: מֵתִיב רַב נָתָן אֲבוּהּ דְּרַב הוּנָא (בַּר נָתָן):
phrases.english: Rav Natan, father of Rav Huna bar Natan, raised an objection:
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the words in round brackets, בַּר נָתָן.

phrases.english: 'But you shall not eat it' –
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:24. This is the same phrase used back in Step 4.

phrases.english: I only know this about fat
that is forbidden to eat but allowed for benefit;

phrases.aramaic: חֵלֶב שֶׁל שׁוֹר הַנִּסְקָל וְעֶגְלָה עֲרוּפָה –
phrases.english: the fat of an ox that is stoned and of a calf whose neck was broken –
from where do we know it?

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵתִיב רַב נָתָן אֲבוּהּ דְּרַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a challenge to רב דימי's statement that the עגלה ערופה is טהור.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב דימי's claim, from the school of רבי ינאי, that the עגלה ערופה is טהור.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא discusses the fat of an עגלה ערופה when talking about נבלה טומאה. That seems to treat the calf as able to be a נבלה; the full argument follows next.

steps.title: The ברייתא's source: 'all fat'
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers its own question. The word 'כל' in 'כל חלב' includes the fat of a שור הנסקל and an עגלה ערופה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'all fat.'
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes the ברייתא that רב נתן started quoting in step 12. It gives the source for including the fat of a שור הנסקל and an עגלה ערופה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא asked how we know the rule of forbidden fat being טהור also covers animals you may not benefit from. Its answer is the extra word 'כל' (all), which widens the rule to every kosher animal. This sets up רב נתן's challenge in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse teaches; introduces a proof from a פסוק
All; an extra word that widens the rule
Forbidden fat of a kosher animal

phrases.english: The verse says:
"All fat."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 3:17. The word 'all' is what brings in the fat of the שור הנסקל and the עגלה ערופה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא quoted by רב נתן in step 12 by giving its answer.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How do we know the rule that forbidden fat is טהור also covers a שור הנסקל and an עגלה ערופה?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word 'כל' in 'כל חלב' includes them.

steps.title: If the calf is טהור, why would its fat need a verse?
steps.stepSummary: רב נתן challenges רב דימי. If the עגלה ערופה itself is טהור, it is obvious that its fat is טהור, so the ברייתא's derivation would be pointless.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you think an עגלה ערופה is טהור, would it make sense that it is טהור but its fat is טמא?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב נתן uses the ברייתא to attack רב דימי's claim from step 11 that the עגלה ערופה is טהור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A פסוק is only needed to teach something we would not have known on our own. If the calf itself is טהור, nobody would think its fat is טמא. So the fact that the ברייתא needs a verse suggests the calf itself is not טהור, which goes against רב דימי.

keyTerms.meaning: It enters your mind; you might think
Pure; does not give off טומאה
Impure; gives off טומאה

steps.confusionAlert: רב נתן is not arguing about the fat itself. Everyone agrees the fat is טהור. He is attacking the claim that the whole calf is טהור.

phrases.english: And if it enters your mind
that an עגלה ערופה is pure,
would it be pure and its fat impure?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ עֶגְלָה עֲרוּפָה טְהוֹרָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the challenge out of the ברייתא completed in step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב דימי's claim (step 11) that the עגלה ערופה is טהור
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the calf is טהור, the fat being טהור is obvious, so the ברייתא's verse would be unnecessary. Its need for a verse implies the calf is not טהור.

steps.title: The verse is needed for a calf that was slaughtered
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the verse is not needed when the calf's neck was broken properly. It is needed for a case where the calf was slaughtered instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where its neck was broken, the verse was not needed. Where it was needed is where the calf was slaughtered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב דימי by narrowing the case the ברייתא is talking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב דימי's rule that the calf is טהור applies when its neck was broken, because that act is what the Torah calls כפרה. If someone slaughtered it instead, that reason does not apply. So the verse is needed to teach that the fat is still טהור in that case.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually broke its neck, the proper act for this calf
It was not needed
Kosher slaughter by cutting the throat

phrases.english: Where he actually broke its neck,
the verse was not needed for it;
where it was needed
is where he actually slaughtered it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכָא דַּעֲרַף מִיעְרָף לָא אִיצְטְרִיכָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב נתן's challenge in step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the ברייתא to a specific case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא was talking about a calf whose neck was broken, which would make the verse pointless if the calf were טהור.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is talking about a calf that was slaughtered, where the calf's own טהרה from neck-breaking does not apply.

steps.title: Slaughter itself should already make it טהור
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: kosher slaughter normally keeps an animal from becoming a נבלה. So in the slaughter case too, the verse seems unnecessary.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let the slaughter help it, to make it pure from being a נבלה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave in step 15.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Slaughter is what normally stops a dead animal from being a טמא נבלה. If the slaughtered calf is not a נבלה, its fat is obviously טהור. So the verse is still not needed, and the question against רב דימי comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it be effective; let it help
To make it pure
An animal that died without kosher slaughter, which is טמא

phrases.english: But let the slaughter be effective for it
to purify it from the status of a נבלה!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתֵיהָנִי לֵיהּ שְׁחִיטָה לְטַהֲרָהּ מִידֵּי נְבֵלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the ברייתא is about a slaughtered calf
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Slaughter already prevents נבלה status, so the slaughtered calf and its fat would be טהור anyway. The verse would still be unnecessary.

steps.title: The verse is needed for a calf that died
steps.stepSummary: The final answer: the verse is needed for an עגלה ערופה that died on its own. Even though the calf itself becomes a נבלה, its fat is still טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed for a case where the calf died.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new case for the ברייתא, which finally explains why the verse is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A calf that simply died had neither neck-breaking nor slaughter, so it is a טמא נבלה. Here we really might think its fat is טמא too, so the verse 'כל חלב' is needed to teach that the fat is טהור. The ברייתא no longer contradicts רב דימי.

keyTerms.meaning: No, it is needed (for a different case)
That died on its own

steps.whatToRemember: רב דימי's view that the עגלה ערופה is טהור stands. The ברייתא's verse is about a calf that died and became a נבלה, and it teaches that even then its fat is טהור.
steps.whyThisMatters: This closes רב נתן's challenge. That means רבי ירמיה's question from step 9, which assumed the עגלה ערופה is טהור, still has a firm basis.

phrases.english: No, it is needed
where it died.
phrases.notes: The calf died before anyone broke its neck or slaughtered it, so it is a נבלה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 16 and finally resolves רב נתן's challenge from step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Moving the ברייתא to a different case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא was about a slaughtered calf, which slaughter would already make טהור.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about a calf that died and is a נבלה. The verse teaches that its fat is still טהור, so there is no proof against רב דימי.

steps.title: Is the calf forbidden even while alive?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא draws an inference from the last answer: if a calf that died before its neck was broken is already forbidden, that means it was forbidden while still alive.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does that mean the עגלה ערופה is forbidden even while it is alive?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices what the last answer implies and asks whether it really means that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 17, the case was an עגלה ערופה that died on its own, before its neck was broken, and the calf was still treated as forbidden. So the forbidden status must have started before the neck-breaking, while the calf was alive. The גמרא asks: is that really so?

keyTerms.meaning: By inference, from this we learn
While still alive
Forbidden (here: forbidden to get any benefit from)

phrases.english: By inference, is it forbidden while alive?
phrases.notes: "It" is the עגלה ערופה. The calf in Step 17 died before its neck was broken, yet it was still treated as forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws out what the final answer of Step 17 implies.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether an עגלה ערופה becomes forbidden for benefit while it is still alive, before its neck is broken.

steps.title: Yes, going down to the valley makes it forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers yes. רבי ינאי heard there is a point at which the calf becomes forbidden but forgot what it is. The scholars said that point is when the calf is brought down to the valley.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes. רבי ינאי said: I heard there is a point at which it becomes forbidden, but I forgot it. The group of scholars said: its going down to the hard valley is what makes it forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says yes, the calf is forbidden while alive. It then tells us exactly when that starts: once the calf is brought down to the valley.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer agrees with the inference from Step 18. רבי ינאי adds a specific moment: the forbidden status does not wait for the neck-breaking. It begins once the calf goes down to the נחל איתן, so a calf that dies after that point is already forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes
A boundary, the point at which something takes effect
The group of scholars
The hard (rough) valley where the calf's neck is broken

steps.whatToRemember: An עגלה ערופה becomes forbidden for benefit while still alive, once it is brought down to the נחל איתן.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains how the calf in Step 17 could already be forbidden even though it died before its neck was broken.

phrases.english: Yes.
Rabbi Yannai said:
I heard the boundary, but I forgot it,
phrases.notes: He means he heard there is a set point at which the calf becomes forbidden, but he forgot what it is.

phrases.english: and the scholars were inclined to say:
its going down to the hard valley is what makes it forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 18 and supports the answer with רבי ינאי.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes, the calf is forbidden while alive, starting from when it is brought down to the נחל איתן.

steps.title: הדרן — Closing פרק חטאת העוף
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula marks the end of the פרק called חטאת העוף.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, פרק חטאת העוף.
steps.whatsHappening: This line closes the chapter. It is not part of the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying הדרן at the end of a פרק shows that we hope to come back and learn it again. The topic changes completely after this line.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you (said at the end of a chapter)
Bird sin offering, the name of the chapter now ending

phrases.english: We will return to you, chapter of the bird sin offering

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter after the final discussion.

steps.title: Sacrifices mixed with animals forbidden for benefit must all die
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה rules that if sacrifices get mixed with animals that are forbidden for any benefit, like a חטאת left to die or a שור הנסקל, all of them must die, even if there is only one forbidden animal in ten thousand.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If any sacrifices got mixed in with sin offerings that are left to die, or with an ox that is to be stoned, even one in ten thousand, all of them must be left to die.
steps.whatsHappening: A new chapter opens with a משנה about sacrifices that got mixed up with forbidden animals. The first case is the strictest one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The forbidden animals here are ones no one may benefit from at all. Because each animal is a separate, important item, the forbidden one does not get cancelled out even in a huge majority. Since we cannot tell which animal is which, none of them can be offered or used, so all must be left to die.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for מתניתין: our משנה
Got mixed together
Sin offerings that are left to die and may never be offered
An ox sentenced to stoning (for killing a person)
Ten thousand

steps.confusionAlert: Usually something forbidden gets cancelled out in a big majority. Here it does not, even at one in ten thousand, so all the animals must die.

phrases.english: Mishnah:
All the offerings that got mixed
with sin offerings that are left to die
or with an ox that is to be stoned,
even one in ten thousand –
they must all die.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ כׇּל הַזְּבָחִים שֶׁנִּתְעָרְבוּ בְּחַטָּאוֹת הַמֵּתוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the new chapter after the הדרן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sacrifices mixed with animals forbidden for any benefit (חטאות המתות, שור הנסקל) are never cancelled out, even at one in ten thousand. All of them must be left to die.

steps.title: Second case begins: mixed with an ox used for a sin
steps.stepSummary: The משנה starts a new case: sacrifices mixed with an ox that was used to commit a sin. The list and the ruling continue in the next section.
steps.simpleTranslation: If they got mixed with an ox that was used to commit a sin, or...
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה is setting up its next case, a milder kind of forbidden animal. The text stops mid-list, and the ruling comes in the next section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An ox used for a sin may not be offered on the מזבח, but people may still benefit from it. Because this kind of animal is less strict than the first group, we should expect a different, more lenient ruling here.

keyTerms.meaning: An ox that was used to commit a sin, which makes it unfit to be a sacrifice

phrases.aramaic: נִתְעָרְבוּ בְּשׁוֹר שֶׁנֶּעֶבְדָה בּוֹ עֲבֵירָה, אוֹ
phrases.english: If they got mixed with an ox that was used for a sin, or

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from animals forbidden for any benefit to animals that are only unfit to be offered.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Opens the case of sacrifices mixed with animals that are unfit for the מזבח but not forbidden for benefit. The ruling follows in the next section.
